sources.title: Delaware Nation: History
sources.note: Direct tribal history, overview, clan leadership, Walking Purchase and contemporary nations. Its broad glyphic-writing assertion and exact ancient population duration are not adopted.

sources.title: Delaware Tribe of Indians: Lenape Family
sources.note: Direct one-page teaching sheet with Herbert C. and John T. Kraft illustration. Educational reconstruction explicitly distinguished from an excavated named house. Upload folder date is not date of historical practices.

sources.title: Delaware Tribe of Indians: Foods
sources.note: Direct three-page community teaching sheet, food processing and storage. Modern frybread not projected into the precontact period.

sources.title: Delaware Tribe of Indians: Lenape Fishing
sources.note: Direct two-page teaching sheet; Kraft reconstructions of spring shad fishing and preservation.

sources.title: Delaware Tribe of Indians: Lenape Canoes
sources.note: Direct two-page teaching sheet, controlled charring and scraping of a dugout. Overbroad statement about beasts of burden elsewhere in North America not used.

sources.title: Jim Rementer: The Lenape Football Game
sources.note: Direct nine-page paper, Nora Thompson Dean’s rules recorded in 1971, pages 5-6. Opening imagined seventeenth-century scene is not treated as an eyewitness record.

sources.title: National Museum of the American Indian: Shoulder bag, 14/3272
sources.note: Original full indexed catalogue: 1740-1770; probably Lenape attribution, deerskin, quills, cones and deer hair. Alleged 1770 New York collecting history kept uncertain.

sources.title: National Museum of the American Indian: Delaware bandolier bag, about 1850
sources.note: Direct object essay, Oklahoma provenance and materials, geometric designs and adaptation of beadwork after removal. Strap may be later.

sources.title: Treaty with the Delawares, September 17, 1778, Smithsonian transcription
sources.note: Original treaty transcription hosted by NMAI, opening and Article III: deputies, troop passage, payment for provisions and protection of families.

sources.title: Lenape Talking Dictionary: wanìshi, entry 10471
sources.note: Direct community dictionary entry, exact word and English translation with audio. Modern spelling; historical orthographic examples are separately dated by dictionary.

sources.title: Pennsylvania Historical and Museum Commission: The Walking Purchase
sources.note: Direct archival deed presentation and historical explanation, prepared route, selected walkers and dispossession. Antiquated descriptions of Native peoples in this archived 2015 text are not adopted.

sources.title: Chinook Indian Nation: Who We Are
sources.note: Direct tribal self-description and five constituent groups. Do not collapse all Chinookan peoples into the present government; no claim all Willapa ancestors spoke a Chinookan language. Conflicting exact constitutional drafting dates on other tribal pages not used.

sources.title: Chinook Indian Nation and Portland State University: By the River
sources.note: Direct community-reviewed collaborative public-history page, Catherine George 1902 account and housing/social hierarchy. Regional house measurements not generalized to all villages. Project authorship confirmed on /chinook/.

sources.title: Ames, Smith, Cornett and Sobel: Cathlapotle investigations, 1991-1996, preliminary report
sources.note: Direct author-hosted late draft of 1999 report, structural remains, faunal assemblage, trade objects. Explicitly regional comparison outside imported coastal outline, not Chinook Nation capital. Preliminary initial founding-date estimates and uncertain iron dates omitted.

sources.title: Chinook Indian Nation and Portland State University: Workhorse of the Columbia
sources.note: Original full indexed collaborative page, practical transport and varied sizes. Exact capacity totals and sacred burial details not needed.

sources.title: Chinook Story: Some of these logs want to become canoes
sources.note: Original full indexed page, carver Tony Johnson’s account of depth pegs, hollowing and steaming; separate explanation of cedar uses.

sources.title: Chinook Story: Lower Columbia historical timeline
sources.note: Original full indexed collaborative timeline, 1830-1831 epidemic and survivor settlements. Precise mortality percentage, shipwreck dating and earliest chronology not adopted.

sources.title: Rachel Lynne Cushman: The 175th Commemoration of Our 1851 Tansy Point Treaties
sources.note: Direct August 7, 2026 tribal scholar essay adapted from dissertation; resistance to removal, unratified treaties, family memories of missing food, 2019 purchase of ten acres. No assertion proposed future restoration facilities are completed.

sources.title: Chinook Indian Nation: Political history
sources.note: Direct tribal chronology, 1851 and 1855 negotiations, 2001 acknowledgement and 2002 reversal. Later litigation outcome not invented.

sources.title: Bureau of Indian Affairs: Chinook judgment funds historical background
sources.note: Direct current agency page checked September 2026; describes Chinook Indian Nation as non-federally recognized, separately identifies Grand Ronde and Siletz. Federal designation not presented as a test of cultural existence.

sources.title: National Park Service: Cathlapotle Plankhouse
sources.note: Direct page, 2005 modern reconstruction, volunteers and educational/community role. No travel opening claim; public closure text is not part of historical narrative. Oversimplified expedition-caused-disease sentence not adopted.

sources.title: Chinook Indian Nation: Language
sources.note: Direct tribal language page identifying Chinuk Wawa as a mixed trade language and recommending Grand Ronde dictionary. Kept distinct from older Chinookan languages.

sources.title: Smithsonian Libraries: Chinuk Wawa dictionary, 2012
sources.note: Full indexed original library catalogue provides exact parallel title and 2012 date; direct request returned 520. Catalogue-normalized spelling explicitly identified, not claimed to reproduce every specialized glyph on the printed cover. Reproducible query: "Chinuk Wawa" "As Our Elders Teach Us" dictionary 2012.

sources.title: Chinook Indian Nation: Our Present
sources.note: Direct community statement, language, stories, songs and ceremonies. Its numerical assertion of unchanged ceremony duration is not adopted.

proposedOverrides.name: Chinook peoples of the lower Columbia

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Broad Lenape historical card, no automatic association with modern state of Delaware or distinct modern tribal IDs. Outline is substantially wider than core homeland and opening warns publicly. Unami and Munsee and separate present governments remain distinguished.

Lower Columbia/coastal regional entry; not all Chinookan peoples absorbed into Chinook Indian Nation. Cathlapotle is explicitly an upriver comparative site outside imported outline. Five contemporary constituent groups named without asserting all their ancestors shared one language. Chinuk Wawa example explicitly modern Grand Ronde dictionary title, catalogue-normalized orthography.
batchIdentityNotes.currentStatusChecked: BIA original historical-background page and tribal political-history page, September 2026. No assertion of final resolution of litigation.
